name: NITE LIGHT CIC
description:
Cleveland is an area in the north-east of England covering 4 districts; Middlesbrough, Redcar, Hartlepool and Stockton-On-Tees. The area is highly industrialised and urbanised with a population of 541,333 (last recorded in 1991). Middlesbrough has the highest numbers of homeless people across the North East of England; our activities will provide benefit to these homeless people through other members of the public buying items through our App. They will have food, drinks, clothes, sleeping bags and other essential items - in turn this will reduce begging on the streets which can make people feel uncomfortable when going about their daily business especially with town centres; we will help to reduce this, contributing to the community as a whole. Outdoor smoke alarms will help to further protect communities as a whole from arson and deliberate fires throughout Cleveland. It costs the councils and the fire service thousands each year as they are unaware that fires have started in derelict buildings or throughout the greener environment. Services throughout the community will benefit as early detection will help to save buildings and green spaces. Also the general public will benefit; burnt buildings and landscapes can look unsightly and really effect the community spirit so as a whole we will be looking to benefit the community. Both services will increase volunteering opportunities giving people valuable skills, new friends, a sense of purpose and increase chances of employment. New job and apprentice opportunities will be brought to the area; increasing employment throughout Cleveland. We will be looking to collaborate with other organisations to regenerate old run down historical buildings to increase the health and wellbeing of the most vulnerable in society such as the terminally ill. Our services will run within Cleveland to start with and then expand to UK wide.

Community benefit - whether it be training and courses for volunteers and staff or opening the services up to be able to offer a homeless person a night in a bed and breakfast or paying for vital identification documents such as birth certificates. The outdoor smoke alarms could be offered to more places of benefit such as allotments, sheds and farm buildings where there is no electricity and too far away for people to hear a standard smoke alarm.
